turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - cdft_piezo_d_eg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format), `d_ij` (the
    piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij|, in pC/N) and `band_gap` (the
    band gap, in eV).
  - cdft_piezo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose
    properties are NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the LARGEST
piezoelectric strain coefficient max|d_ij| (in pC/N) that also satisfy a
low-leakage requirement: the band gap must be at least 5 eV. Band gaps are
NOT given for the pool -- you must infer them. A selected candidate whose
band gap is below the threshold scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set shows that large max\(|d_{ij}|\) coexists with \(E_g\ge5\) eV only for a few chemical families: perchlorates/chlorates (\(\mathrm{RbClO_4}\), \(d\approx25\)), cyanamides (\(\mathrm{CdC_2N_2}\), \(d\approx29\)), hydroxides (\(\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}\), \(d\approx15\)), and selected phosphates/silicates (\(d\approx6{-}13\)). All other high-\(d\) chemistries (iodides, sulfides, heavy-metal half-Heuslers, etc.) have gaps well below the 5 eV cutoff.

Inspection of the pool structures and compositions immediately isolates the same families:

- c072 (\(\mathrm{NaClO_3}\), \(P2_13\)) is the direct analogue of the training perchlorates and is therefore expected to be the strongest piezoelectric that still satisfies the gap constraint.
- c063 (\(\mathrm{CN_2}\)) belongs to the same cyanamide family that produces the largest training \(d\) values while retaining \(E_g>7\) eV.
- c079 (\(\mathrm{Be(OH)_2}\)) is isostructural with the training hydroxide that already meets both targets.
- c005 (cyclophosphate) and c038 (gehlenite) are the wide-gap tetrahedral oxides whose training counterparts give the next-highest \(d\) values.

All other pool entries are either centrosymmetric, contain gap-reducing cations (Zn, Cd, Ga, Bi, \ldots), or belong to families whose training \(d\) is \(\lesssim5\,\mathrm{pC\,N^{-1}}\). Consequently the five candidates above, ranked by expected max\(|d_{ij}|\), are the only ones that simultaneously maximise the piezoelectric coefficient and obey the leakage constraint.

Final: c072, c063, c079, c005, c038
